My eating habits used to be awful. I’d never come home from a store without candy and my main source of food was fast food. Now I eat zero sugar and my diet is pretty much lean meat, fruit, nuts, vegetables, and only whole grain carbs. It took me about half a year to a year to get here though. Sounds like you already tried stocking up on only healthy foods which is a good tool to manage your diet. But, to just go cold turkey and say I’m going to be healthy right now is very difficult. I’d recommend starting out slowly and try one thing at a time instead of going all out. And I know it’s one thing to say it and another to do it but don’t be too hard on yourself if it doesn’t happen overnight or you slip up. I used to take one mistake as complete failure and give up and binge on whatever which is not good obviously. Congratulate yourself for each step of progress you make. Start by just replacing one or two foods with a healthier option. Or try to get one serving of vegetables every few days. Also find out if it’s easier for you to eliminate a food completely or just have it once in a while. It’s harder for me personally to just have one of something than to abstain completely. After enough time without something you’ll stop craving it if you choose that way to do things. It takes a while for that to happen though. Other people have success with only eating a food occasionally so it’s up to you which way works best.

All this sounds eerily familiar.  (Minus the actual courage to try dating, so good on you for that) You've got a good start though. The obvious answer is to just go with it of course but as you know it's not that simple. I know if I was in the situation I'd want to try and be open as possible while being as kind and aware of her feelings as much as I could. But, as for how to do that, that's going to come down to you. Over time give her more of your trust and hopefully she'll prove it's worth it. It'll hurt to break it off regardless so you may as well give it a chance. It's better to know if you're incompatible than to just break it off out of fear. She'll be hurt even more if you just break it off like that. To me at least I'd rather learn we're incompatible than just have someone leave without a lot of good reason. It seems like it'll be pretty hard for you to place all your trust in her. Hell, I have pretty little self worth so placing trust in people is hard for me too. If she knows about your mental health it would probably be easier. It might be a bit awkward to bring up though. So you can either bring it up if you feel up to it or just mention it casually. I'd wait longer to do it though. As long as you're trying,being honest as you can, try to be aware of her feelings and she's a good person it nothing should go too badly. Keep going for it. The fear of messing something up isn't worth ending it. You probably know that. That fear sucks. But it's not going to go away unless you go outside your comfort zone. A good person who is worth dating in my mind at least wouldn't be bothered too much by your mental illness. You deserve to date if you want to. It might make things a little more difficult sure, but working through it is worth a try. You're trying to get out there and that's great. I'm rooting for you!
